signals.title: NOK/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Crude Shock
signals.text: NOK leads the weekly G10 currency strength scorecard with an average gain of +1.679% across 2 pairs, while USD trails as the laggard at -0.932% across 9 pairs, opening a critical 2.610% bilateral spread. Geopolitical tension in the Middle East has pushed Brent crude toward $120 resistance, providing a potent terms-of-trade catalyst for the petro-currency. USD/NOK trades at 9.316 with a downtrend firmly in force below its SMA20 of 9.503 and SMA200 of 9.514, currently extended 2.38 ATR below the short-term average. Meanwhile, retail sentiment shows an extreme 100% net long positioning in USD/NOK, setting up an asymmetric capitulation risk against the prevailing institutional flow. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK, following the commodity-backed bilateral theme and retail positioning overhang. Catalyst: US Durable Goods Orders at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Brent crude retreats sharply from $120 resistance, stalling NOK outperformance.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Real Rate Drag
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1220, pinned beneath its descending SMA20 at 1.1238 and SMA50 at 1.1440. Options markets display an elevated volatility premium, with 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.7% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.1%, generating a notable +2.5% vol risk premium. Macro policy spreads continue to limit upside, as Fed policy at 4.00% versus ECB at 2.65% maintains a 135bp carry advantage in favor of the dollar, reinforced by a +146bp SOFR-€STR spread. Leveraged fund positioning reflects this drag, with net short contracts at -94,138 representing the 2nd percentile of its 52-week historical distribution. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, constrained by carry disadvantage and negative technical momentum. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech at 17:00 UTC. Risk: Germany Ifo expectations print well above the 90.4 consensus, triggering an algorithmic short-squeeze.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Policy Divergence + Technical Reversal
signals.text: AUD/USD prints at 0.7032, breaking above its SMA20 of 0.6980 and testing short-term resistance near its descending SMA50 at 0.7078. The underlying policy backdrop has turned supportive following hawkish rhetoric from RBA Assistant Governor Hunter, positioning the RBA at 4.60% against the Fed at 4.00% for a 60bp cash carry advantage and a 70bp AONIA-SOFR yield premium. CFTC data confirms Leveraged Funds have added +2,628 contracts WoW to reach a net long of +47,606 contracts, while 2Y yield spreads sit at +8bp in Australia's favor. Despite Australia's negative ESI index of -5.7, the pair's price structure has established a breakout above the prior 10-day high. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD, supported by carry premium and short-term technical reversal. Catalyst: RBA Policy Meeting on 3 Nov. Risk: Broad equity weakness accelerates, undermining commodity beta and halting the technical recovery.
